items.statement: EBITDA margin target: 16.5%-17%
items.quote: Overall, like I had mentioned earlier, we think around 16.5% – 17% EBITDA is a good position today.

items.statement: Ongoing labour code impact estimated at $150K-$200K/quarter
items.quote: We don't expect a significant impact on our books going forward. When we assess that impact, I think it was around $150,000 to $200,000 per quarter

items.statement: Offering 15%-30% productivity savings to clients over 3-year outcome-based contracts
items.quote: we have closed a few deals where we have moved our customers from time and material to an outcome -based contract and also offeri ng anywhere between a 15% to 30% savings on productivity over a 3-year tenure

items.statement: Passing 5%-10% productivity benefits to U.K. Public Sector clients during renewals
items.quote: we had passed almost 5% to 10% benefit to our customers when we got them into renewal last year.

items.statement: U.K. government expects 15%+ efficiency across projects
items.quote: there is also continued pressure from the government to at least deliver a 15% or higher efficiency across all government projects.

items.statement: Strong global demand in Healthcare/Life Sciences (U.K., U.S., AMEA)

items.statement: U.S. market expected to improve sustainably in FY27

items.statement: Middle East revenue delayed by contract signing delays (expected in Jan FY27)
items.quote: We are confident that we will get the order in, and we are hoping that it will come in January itself.

items.statement: U.K. Public Sector margin pressure due to budget shifts to Healthcare/Defence
items.quote: there is margin pressures on some of our accounts as the government expects to shift their budget into Healthcare and reduce some of their spending in some of the other government departments.

items.statement: Subcontracting costs may rise temporarily for new U.S. deals
items.quote: as we look at getting into execution, some of these deals initially may see higher subcontracting costs.

items.statement: Global advances growth guidance for FY26
items.quote: the guidance for global advances growth will be around 13 -14%, and global deposit growth around will be around 11 -12% for FY26.

items.statement: RAM advances growth outlook for FY27
items.quote: we are very much positive and buoyant and we feel that from the Top Management side also for FY 27, we will give a very good RAM growth.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY26 and Q4 FY26
items.quote: for FY 26, though, we are at 2.57% as on 31st December for the annualized FY26 we hope that we should be maintaining a NIM of around 2.50% and for the Q4, we should be somewhere around 2.60%.

items.statement: Gold loan LTV reduced to 75% from 85-90%
items.quote: we have reduced the loan to value to 75% now. So, any fresh Q3 FY26 Earnings Call Transcript January 21, 2026 8 advances in the gold loan category, we are keeping a margin of 25% as against earlier of 10 % or 15

items.statement: RAM demand outlook driven by economy and income growth
items.quote: the way Indian economy is growing, the way the income levels are growing, both in the cities and also in the agriculture side, we see not much impact on the RAM growth.

items.statement: RAM book target at 65% of advances by FY2031
items.quote: our total business should be at around Rs.31 Lac crore; Within that number within the credit number, the RAM book should be at around 65% and 35% has to be corporate.

items.statement: International advances target at 15-16% of global advances by FY2031
items.quote: our international book should be at around 15 to 16% of the global book on the advances side.

items.statement: Gold loan risk due to rising gold prices
items.quote: definitely it may pose a risk particularly with respect to the valuations which are there on the metal.

items.statement: SMA-2 driven by 3 state government accounts with guarantees
items.quote: the majority of that in the SMA -2 categories are three State Government accounts which are there which are backed by the State Government guarantee also.

items.statement: Fresh slippages driven by one corporate road account
items.quote: One of the main reasons is that there was one corporate road account which slipped into NPA, that is the reason it's a consortium account.

items.statement: IT capex as % of operating expenses
items.quote: nearly 10% of the Op ex is going to the IT Opex.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA breakeven for Ascelis Peptides
items.quote: we remain confident, and we are on track to get to that position.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA neutrality for Ascelis Peptides
items.quote: our target is always to turn positive from next financial year.

items.statement: US revenue growth of $40M–$50M annually
items.quote: That's what we aspire for and we are confident of that.

items.statement: Incremental revenue from Genome Valley facility launches
items.quote: we'll start this quarter, and we'll see an incremental revenue coming up.

items.statement: 3–4 controlled substance launches in next 1.5 years
items.quote: we have about 3 launches, and they will -- 3 to 4 launches, and they will contribute to a very meaningful percentage of our overall growth story

items.statement: System enhancements capex/opex over coming quarters
items.quote: we expect to invest into system enhancements, which will involve some capex and opex over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 meaningful improvement in Ascelis Peptides performance
items.quote: Q4 is tracking towards a meaningful improvement in performance, supported by ongoing project deliveries.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement from better product mix
items.quote: gross margin improved with a better product mix for the finished dosage segment.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement from sales growth and margin expansion
items.quote: The improvement in EBITDA was primarily due to sales growth and margin expansion.

items.statement: Sequential improvement in sales and margins expected
items.quote: we are looking at sequential improvement, both on the sales and margin side.

items.statement: Paracetamol price erosion observed
items.quote: we do see some amount of price erosion also in paracetamol.

items.statement: Paracetamol demand increasing from key customers
items.quote: we are seeing an increase in demand from our key customers in both APIs, PFIs and finished dosages.

items.statement: Complex generics contribution to revenue grew from 27% to 49% YoY
items.quote: Q3 FY '25 to '26, we grew from 27% as a total contribution to 49%.

items.statement: Shift toward complex generics and controlled substances
items.quote: we plan on filing a certain number of products more inclined towards complex generics in the future.

items.statement: Gagillapur remediation timeline uncertain
items.quote: we cannot put a timeline to that, but we will be submitting the response quite early in the very near future.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance for FY26 maintained at 12-14% despite 9M achievement of ~11% due to muted corporate growth and PSU exposure reduction.

items.statement: Corporate credit pipeline: ₹4,000-5,000 crore unavailed, ₹8,000-9,000 crore in pipeline; total ₹10,000-12,000 crore available.
items.quote: Yeah-yeah. Sushil ji, in case of corporate credit, almost ₹4,000-₹5,000 crores are unavailed, in pipeline almost ₹8,000-₹9,000 crores in the pipeline. Total ₹10,000-₹12,000 crores available in the corporates.

items.statement: Deposit repricing: 75% done; remaining 25% to be completed in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27.
items.quote: See, around 75% of my d eposit book has been repriced. I think remaining some portion will get repriced in this quarter and maybe one -tenth of the book will be repriced in the first quarter

items.statement: RAM (Retail, Agri, MSME) credit growth expected to continue at 20%+ (Retail: 28%, Agri: 24%, MSME: 23% in Q3 FY26).
items.quote: Similarly, Agri also. Agri also quarter -on-quarter consistently we are growing. This quarter growth was around 23% -24% and previous quarter it was in the range of 17% - 20%. - Similarly, MSME for las t three quarters is more than 20

items.statement: Cross-selling success: 40-50% of loan customers onboarded for additional products (e.g., CASA, FDs, loan against FDs).
items.quote: See, our endeavor is to get at least 1 more product from each customer; our endeavor is that. But definitely not every customer, maybe 40%-50% of the customers we are able to onboard on some other product.

items.statement: Geopolitical risk exposure minimal: ₹100 crore (5% of ₹2,000 crore export credit) in sanctioned countries facing tariffs/sanctions.
items.quote: If I have to look at our banks' exposure, we have around ₹2,000 crore of export credit exposure and of which only 5% is in respect of countries where some tariff and all these things have happened. So, it is not a major one; around ₹100 crore of only exposure for the bank in those countries.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio: ₹15,000 crore (₹4,000 crore retail, ₹10,500 crore Agri); LTV 25-30% (retail), 15-20% (Agri).

And of that, around ₹4,000 crores should be in the retail, ₹4,000+ should be in the retail, and around ₹10,500 crores odd should be in the agriculture

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs. 19,000–21,000 met with 9M average of Rs. 21,300; FY26 full-year average expected around Rs. 21,000
items.quote: whatever guidance we have provided for the year, Rs. 19,000 to 21,000 per metric ton is what we had given. We have delivered in nine months an average of around 21,300 and we believe that this year on an average basis around this number we should be closing.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth guidance met with 9M deliveries up 11% YoY; FY26 full-year guidance expected to hold
items.quote: whatever guidance we had given in terms of volume growth and EBITDA per ton, we are extremely confident of meeting those numbers. It is still because of certain geopolitical situations, QCO relaxation, we would like to stick to this guidance only.

items.statement: FY26 capex of Rs. 2,700 crore; Rs. 2,200 crore spent in 9M, on track to complete FY26 guidance
items.quote: we had given a guidance of 2,700 crores as a CapEx for the whole financial year FY26. 2,200 crores we have already done and we are on course of completing or ending with around 2,700 crores of CapEx in FY26.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong in automotive, ornamental pipe/tube, railways, metro, lift/elevator, white goods; export demand subdued due to geopolitical uncertainty
items.quote: our sales volume in Q3 FY26 grew by 11% year-on-year and remained steady quarter-on-quarter, supported by sustained domestic demand amidst stability in the export market.

items.statement: Export demand uncertain due to geopolitical factors (e.g., Trump policies, CBAM), but domestic demand robust
items.quote: export is a very uncertain situation because of the geopolitical factors. Nothing to do with the company. We are still sticking to our supply chain. We are still supplying our customers. It is more from our customer side because of this lack of clarity.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA up 17% YoY to Rs. 1,408 crore; PAT up 27% YoY to Rs. 828 crore
items.quote: our Q3 consolidated EBITDA increased by around 17% year-on-year and around 1% on quarter-on-quarter to Rs. 1408 crores.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA up 14% YoY to Rs. 4,106 crore; PAT up 23% YoY to Rs. 2,350 crore
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA increased by around 14% year-on-year to Rs. 4106 crores and consolidated PAT stood at Rs. 2350 crores with an increase of around 23% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Stainless steel prices to rise if nickel prices remain high; Q3 realizations impacted by softer nickel prices
items.quote: if the nickel remains on the higher level, the level at which it is, it will definitely lift the average realization than what we attained in Quarter 3.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong in automotive (GST cut), railways (Vande Bharat, metro), white goods (GST cut), and ornamental pipe/tube
items.quote: In the domestic market, JSL performance was consistent, underpinned by the demand momentum from key sectors such as automotive, ornamental pipe and tube, railways, metro, lift and elevator, white goods.

items.statement: QCO relaxation led to import surge; anti-dumping duty (ADD) investigation ongoing; government intervention expected to protect domestic industry
items.quote: QCO relaxation was given, import surges further happened again in the last few months. So, that is another area that we are constantly picking up with the ministry that a lot of circumvention is happening, import surge has happened. So, QCO is definitely required for the entire industry.

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs. 1 per share (Rs. 82.44 crore total) approved for FY26; record date January 29, 2026
items.quote: The Board of Directors have approved an interim dividend payment for FY26 of Rs. 1 per share with a face value of Rs. 2 each, aggregating to a payout of nearly Rs. 82.44 crores.

items.statement: NPI venture (Indonesia) nickel capacity: 14,000 tons (50% share); Q3 FY26 EBITDA per ton at Rs. 900; FY26 guidance: Rs. 500–1,500 per ton
items.quote: we had given a guidance of around $500 to $1 ,500 range for metric ton of nickel. And Quarter 3, we have hit somewhere around $900. And we expect , if the nickel prices remain high, so we should be on the higher side of this range

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth of 24%-25% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: If the prices remain at current level. Even if they don't go up from here but they consolidate, then we will see very strong growth in the gold loan portfolio. Vedant Sarda: 25%, 26% growth on Q-o-Q basis? Nirmal Jain: Yes. That should be a very comfortable

items.statement: Housing loan AUM growth of 15%-16% in FY27
items.quote: So, on the book, we plan to grow by about 15%-16%. And on disbursement, it will be 24%-25%.

items.statement: Overall AUM growth of 20%-25% in FY27
items.quote: On the whole, you should see about 20%-25% AUM growth next year.

items.statement: ROE target of 18%-20% in next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, our ROE was in the range of 18% to 20% in normal times. So, we would endeavor to reach towards that.

items.statement: Leverage to be maintained around 4-4.5x
items.quote: Our leverage, we will keep it around 4-4.5, and capital adequacy, we would like it to be closer to 20.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 26% quarter-on-quarter and 189% year-on-year
items.quote: Gold, in particular, grew by around 26% quarter-on-quarter and around 189% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Gold loan tonnage grew 7% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: There is about 7% increase tonnage-wise also.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM crossed pre-embargo level at INR 43,432 crore
items.quote: Gold loan, which crossed the pre-embargo level at INR 43,432 crores, supported by a healthy gross NPA of 0.36%.

items.statement: Gold loan Stage-3 provision reduced from 42% to 19% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Stage-3 losses are always, again, dependent on gold prices as well as your historical. So, the way ECL is computed is based on empirical data. And what we have seen is that our losses have been negligible.

items.statement: No PLR changes in housing book
items.quote: No, no. We did not do anything. No change.

items.statement: Strong demand momentum in gold loans due to higher LTV and clampdown on unsecured loans
items.quote: Markets are very strong because loan -to-value has gone up. The addressable market's capacity to borrow has gone up significantly because of gold prices, one. Two, there has been a clampdown on the unsecured MSME and personal loan, and many of these customer s are also basically moving towards gold

items.statement: Shift to affordable and emerging segments in housing loans
items.quote: Our focus, I think, going forward is going to be in terms of segments broadly on emerging and affordable. Affordable largely will be the priority for us, which can give us yield and emerging to asset mix, which can help us in terms of growth

items.statement: No financial impact from income tax special audit; no tax demand, penalty, or adjudication
items.quote: There is no tax demand, no penalty, and no determination against the company pursuant to this direction. At this stage, there is no financial impact that can be ascertained.

items.statement: No capital raising plans announced; monitoring leverage and capital adequacy
items.quote: At this stage, we haven't announced any capital raising plan. We are monitoring the situation very carefully. But whenever appropriate, we will raise capital.

items.statement: Power demand growth robust at 6.5% YoY in Dec 2025, 6% in Jan 2026 (first 20 days)
items.quote: power demand growth in December 2025 was robust at 6.5% year on year, driven primarily by strong industrial activity. Even for the first 20 days of January 2026, power demand growth is robust at 6%.

items.statement: Power demand growth muted at 0.5% YoY for YTD Dec 2025 due to weather
items.quote: For the year-to-date period until December 2025, overall power demand growth stood at a modest 0.5% year on year.

items.statement: 18.7 GW incremental generation capacity and 29.6 GW-hour storage capacity locked in
items.quote: We have already locked in about 18.7 GW of incremental capacity in generation and 29.6 GW hour in storage, which will take our installed capacity beyond our stated target of 30 GW in generation while we are confident of achieving our 40 GW hour in storage by 2030.

items.statement: 10-12 GW Renewable Generation PPA signed in first 9 months FY26
items.quote: for the first 9 months of the fiscal, about 10-12 GW of Renewable Generation PPA is estimated to have signed

items.statement: 12.6 GW renewable capacity already contracted with PPAs signed
items.quote: if you see that our total capacity, which is there logged in, it's 12.6 GW of capacity, which is already contracted, already PPA signed, in the RE front.

items.statement: 4.5 GW renewable capacity pending PPA closure
items.quote: there is a total capacity, which is there is about 4.5 GW for which there is pendencies.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 pending finalization
items.quote: Regarding the capex numbers, as and when we finalize our plan for next year—which we will be doing shortly—we will definitely make the announcement at the right time.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 on track for 1.5 GW capacity addition in H2
items.quote: we are well on track. And in the current quarter, the capacity additions, which are going to take place, we will be meeting the guidance what we have given for 1.5 GW in second half of current fiscal.

items.statement: ₹3,000 crore promoter equity infusion (₹500 crore equity + ₹2,500 crore warrants)

items.statement: Up to ₹10,000 crore QIP approval received
items.quote: consistent with last year, we have also received Shareholder’s approval for a potential issuance of up to ₹10,000 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement.

items.statement: Merchant power realizations at 20% premium to exchange prices in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Despite this, our merchant realizations were at 20% premium to the average exchange prices.

items.quote: it is encouraging to note the improvement in the merchant tariffs by about 30% in the first 21 days of January compared to the average tariffs in the previous quarter.

items.quote: For the first bid the tariff is in the range of ₹3.65, which we have already announced. And the second ₹4.06. This is a fixed charge only.

items.statement: Utkal PPA tariff ₹5.8/unit (fixed + variable)
items.quote: this is a fixed tariff of ₹5.8. Of course, scalable, but this ₹5.8 tariff is the year 1 tariff, which we are going to get from Karnataka.

items.statement: KSK tariff reduction of ₹1.25/unit in FY27
items.quote: there will be a tariff reduction of close to about ₹1.25 from one of the DISCOMs, so that will definitely have some impact.

items.statement: Power demand growth long-term intact despite near-term weather-led softness
items.quote: we firmly believe the long-term demand growth story remains intact, and the current softness is largely a weather-led phenomenon.

items.statement: Thermal capacity bids aggregated 12.8 GW in first 9 months FY26
items.quote: On the thermal front, bids from various states aggregated 12.8 GW during the first nine months of the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Renewable energy bidding moderated to 10.4 GW in first 9 months FY26
items.quote: renewable energy bidding activity has moderated with only 10.4 GW for the first nine months of this fiscal.

items.statement: Storage bids observed 7.6 GW in first 9 months FY26 vs 1.6 GW in FY25
items.quote: Further, 7.6 GW of storage bids were observed in the first nine months compared to 1.6 GW of storage bidding in FY25.

items.statement: Curtailment impact negligible; temporary grid connectivity curtailment reduced post new evacuation
items.quote: the impact on us is negligible right now. And the positive which has happened, just maybe a week or 10 days back, the new evacuation this connectivity has got started. With this, - the curtailment has significantly reduced

items.statement: Renewable capacity additions (3.1 GW) and thermal capacity additions (2.1 GW) in past 12 months
items.quote: Over the past twelve months, we have added 5.2 GW of capacity, comprising 3.1 GW of renewables and 2.1 GW of thermal.

items.statement: 125 MW new capacity added in Q3 FY26 (renewables + hybrids)
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 125 MW of new capacity, in renewables, including hybrid projects.

items.statement: 3.3 GW (25% of installed capacity) secured with Group Captive and C&I customers
items.quote: On the capacity front, approximately 3.3 GW which forms around 25% of our current installed capacity is secured with high-quality Group Captive and C&I customers.

items.statement: Renewables tied up at blended average tariff of ₹3.65/unit
items.quote: these capacities are contracted at highly remunerative tariffs—with renewables tied up at a high blended average tariff of over ₹3.65 per unit.

items.statement: Promoter equity infusion expected to improve credit rating
items.quote: definitely, we expect—just as the market does—that the Promoter increasing their stake at current levels is a positive signal. This is being viewed favourably both by the market and by the rating agencies.

items.statement: ROA to reach 1% by March 2027
items.quote: we think that ROA of 1% is surely possible by the end of March ‘27.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to improve to 50-55% by March 2027 (from 60.84% in Q3 FY26)
items.quote: by the end of March 27, we should be nearly around between 50% to 55%.

items.statement: IT spend of Rs.900 crore over last 3 years
items.quote: In the last three years, we have an approved outlay of Rs.900 crores in IT.

items.statement: Corporate credit pipeline of Rs.20,000 crore (undisbursed + proposals under consideration)
items.quote: The overall pipeline so far is Rs.20,000 crore.

items.statement: NIM to stabilize and bottom out by Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27
items.quote: the NIM, will get bottomed out by the end of this quarter or maximum by the end of the next quarter.

items.statement: NIM to improve via asset mix shift (Retail, Agri, MSME) and fee income growth
items.quote: we churn our assets book into the various segments and also increase our fee income to that.

items.statement: Credit demand strong (advances grew 15.05% YoY in Q3 FY26)
items.quote: Advances grew by 15.05% and the same stood at Rs.1,10,297 Crore.

items.statement: Digital loan growth: 40% of home loans and 54% of car loans sanctioned digitally in Q3 FY26
items.quote: digital home loans during the quarter of December ‘25, 40% share of the total housing loans sanctioned was digitally or digitally assisted. items.statement: New digital products (solar, commercial vehicle loans, personal loans, gold loans, mutual funds, etc.) to launch by March 2026
items.quote: So these are all lined up at very advanced stages. We expect that by March 2026 most of these will be actually implemented.

items.statement: No immediate delinquency risk in two state government-guaranteed SMA accounts; adequate provisions made
items.quote: We don't foresee any immediate delinquency situation, but however, as a as a precautionary measure and as per the norms we have significantly provided for in these two -state government guaranteed standard accounts

items.statement: Excess provisions (30% and 20%) held in two state government-guaranteed accounts
items.quote: in one of those two state government guaranteed accounts we are having provision of 30% and the other one is at 20%.

items.statement: Deposits (retail term deposits growing at 18.34% YoY in Q3 FY26) to fund credit growth
items.quote: our Retail Term Deposit is growing at around 18% plus and overall the credit growth we are aligning around 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Loan book to grow at 20% CAGR to INR 7,500 crores by FY30

items.statement: PBT to grow at 30% CAGR to INR 500 crores by FY30
items.quote: From the profitability perspective, the CAGR is targeted to be around 30% during the same period, so that we achieve Profit Before Tax of INR 500 crores in FY30.

items.statement: Supply chain financing remains 70% of AUM
items.quote: Supply chain financing, continues to remain our core strength and focus, which presently contributes to around 70% of our AUM.

items.statement: Factoring business to be launched but not significant initially

items.statement: Equity to increase to INR 1,450-1,500 crores by FY27
items.quote: Additional equity of INR 338 crores is expected by April and with accruals of Q4 put together, I think we are looking to have an equity base of somewhere between INR 1,450 crores to INR 1,500 crores as we begin the new financial year.

items.statement: INR 5,000 crores borrowing capacity approved
items.quote: We are currently dealing with 18 banks and two mutual funds for our borrowing. So, we have ample room available with us to grow our balance sheet. If we were to lever age ourselves from 2x to 3x, then the resultant return on equity will also be

items.quote: April is the due timeline, but, we might do it earlier also, although there is no compulsion on the shareholders to do it earlier.

items.statement: Board approved 4 new subsidiaries (ARC, AIF, Insurance Broking, FinTech) at ideation stage

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin per SCM expected in ₹5.5–₹6.5 range

items.statement: Unsecured business loan portfolio run rate at Rs. 20 crores/month
items.quote: unsecured business loan portfolio is growing at a healthy and calibrated pace, which is now clocking a run rate of Rs. 20 crores per month.
